subject: Weekly GPU stewardship & deal handoff (Q3 readiness)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, nora.king@orbitai.com
Cc: cloud-broker@cloudscale.io
Date: 2027-04-18T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Weekly GPU stewardship & deal handoff (Q3 readiness)

Team — kicking off this week's fleet planning thread focused on Q3 readiness for OrbitAI (DEAL-7891) and a couple other large pipeline items. Attached: Q3_pipeline_snapshot.xlsx and provisioning_scenarios.pdf. High level asks and context: 

- OrbitAI is asking to start pilot in mid-July with a 6‑week ramp to 50 reserved GPUs and 100 burst slots. Sales expects revenue recognition in August if we can meet that start.
- We need a clear commit ask by EOD Tue so Finance can confirm budget cadence and Infra can start procurement/burst planning.

Specific asks: 
1) Sales (Laura/Marissa): confirm which deals must be prioritized for reserved capacity vs burst. Highlight date windows and any flexibility.
2) Finance (Ben): confirm any spend guardrails or approval latencies if we move from burst to reserved in month T‑1.
3) Infra (Ben/Marissa): provide realistic provisioning lead times for both reserved pools and burst capacity on CloudScale (include SLA knock-on impacts).

Risks I want surfaced this week: vendor provisioning lag, model-variant memory needs (OrbitAI wants 70B fine-tuned), and competing week‑of-July events that may consume slots.

Proposed meeting: Thu 10:00 PT sync (30m) if we have numbers. If not, I'll collect replies and issue an ops playbook (canary ramp + fallback to hosted).

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Q3_pipeline_snapshot.xlsx (workbook), provisioning_scenarios.pdf (overview)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, nora.king@orbitai.com
Date: 2027-04-18T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly GPU stewardship & deal handoff (Q3 readiness)

Thanks Aditya — quick summary from Sales after looking at the snapshot: 

- OrbitAI: pilot starting mid-July is still the ask. They are flexible +/- 2 weeks but prefer mid-July for go/no-go with their customer. They'd prefer reserved for predictability but can accept a staged ramp (30 reserved -> 50 reserved) if we can guarantee burst between weeks 3–6.
- ACME (smaller pilot): can be pushed to Aug if needed; not critical for Q3 recognition.

Priority for reserved capacity this week (proposed):
• OrbitAI (DEAL-7891) — Priority 1, target 50 reserved by start of production.
• NimbusLabs (internal name: NIM-4) — Priority 2, target 20 reserved but flexible.

I'll mark OrbitAI as anchor and will ask Nora if they can accept a staggered ramp. If they push back I'll escalate.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Director, GTM
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-04-18T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly GPU stewardship & deal handoff (Q3 readiness)

Adding infra/finops perspective and attached fleet_availability.csv with slot timelines. Key notes: 

- Reserved procurement (new hardware or reserved term on CloudScale) typically has a 6–8 week lead time for predictable delivery to our pools. If OrbitAI absolutely needs reserved by mid-July we need commitment by EOD Tue and a signed SOW to start procurement.
- Burst capacity: CloudScale reports availability on demand but not guaranteed for sustained bursts; we can provision short bursts (up to 2 weeks) reliably, anything beyond needs reservation.
- Memory/instance sizing: for 70B fine-tuned weights we need a Q4-like instance shape; if OrbitAI can accept quantized 16-bit variants we reduce memory pressure by ~30%.

Immediate asks from Infra/FinOps: 
1) Sales to confirm whether OrbitAI will sign an SOW this week (even if T&Cs are in redline).
2) If SOW delayed > 10 business days, we should move to a staged-burst plan to avoid stranded procurement spend.

Ben Carter
Director, Cloud Infra and Capacity
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: fleet_availability.csv (CSV)

Hi all — thanks for the clear notes. Quick clarifications from OrbitAI: 

- We can sign an SOW by next Tue (2027-04-26) if the redlines are limited to payment terms; procurement for our side is aligned to that timeline.
- We are open to a staged approach: start with 30 reserved GPUs for pilot, add 20 more in week 3 pending performance. Burst for weeks 3–6 is acceptable as long as we have a documented fallback to hosted in case burst drops below requested levels.
- We will accept a quantized model variant for the pilot if Redwood certifies the quality delta (Nora will coordinate a short eval).

Nora King
Head of Platform Partnerships, OrbitAI
nora.king@orbitai.com

Thanks everyone — quick summary / decisions captured here so we have a single source of truth before Thu sync: 

Decisions: 
• OrbitAI: agree staged ramp — 30 reserved at pilot start (target mid-July), +20 reserved in week 3 on performance and signed milestone. Burst request for weeks 3–6 approved as contingency.
• Finance: Ben to flag any budget approval lags if SOW completes after Tue; we will route a provisional spend authorization if SOW slips >5 business days.
• Infra: Marissa to open procurement ticket with CloudScale (ticket #CS-1259) assuming SOW by 2027-04-26. Provide exact instance shapes by Mon EOD.

Action items (owners):
1) Laura — confirm by EOD Mon with OrbitAI whether they will sign SOW by 2027-04-26 and confirm any non-negotiable terms.
2) Ben — prepare provisional spend authorization flow and confirm whether we can apply a short-term burst escrow if SOW delays.
3) Marissa — open procurement ticket with CloudScale and provide instance shape and expected delivery ETA by Mon EOD.
4) Aditya — draft a short canary ramp playbook (will circulate by Tue morning) that includes fallback to hosted and quality gates for quantized variants.

I'll run the Thu 10:00 PT 30m sync only if we still have open questions after Monday updates; otherwise we'll capture in next week's cadence.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
